# Curated rule files in RULEST CELF

> [← Documentation index](../README.md)


RULEST can add an external Hashcat rule file to the candidate pool used by
**greedy / CELF selection**. Imported rules compete with rules generated by
RULEST; importing a rule does not force it into the selected output. Every
candidate is evaluated by the normal exact marginal-coverage path.

## CLI

```bash
python run_rulest.py BASE.txt TARGET.txt \
  --select-mode greedy \
  --select-budget 5000 \
  --celf-seed-rules curated.rule \
  --celf-seed-max-rules 1000 \
  --output selected.rule
```

Pass `--celf-seed-rules PATH` more than once to import from several files.
The loader keeps file order, so place preferred candidates earlier. The
`--celf-seed-max-rules` value is one shared cap across all supplied files. Its
default is 1,000; any positive integer is accepted, so the cap can be raised
for larger seed libraries. The current CLI requires a value of at least 1.

`--celf-seed-rules` requires `--select-mode greedy`. It is distinct from the
existing `--seed-rules` option, which continues to feed RULEST's Stage S seed
path rather than the CELF candidate pool.

## Import validation

The loader reads text as Latin-1 and processes rules in file order. It excludes
blank lines and full-line comments, and counts invalid entries, duplicates,
entries already present in the generated pool, and rules that exceed the
configured maximum chain depth. A candidate must be ASCII and pass the GPU
rule-compatibility validator; it must also fit the engine's Hashcat chain
limits. Byte-identical rule strings are kept only once.

After loading, imported rules join the other CELF candidates. CELF uses exact
marginal gain against the currently uncovered TARGET set when deciding which
rule wins. Upper bounds may prioritize or prune work, but they do not preselect
a rule. See [`../engineering/RULEST_CELF.md`](../engineering/RULEST_CELF.md) for
the RULEST CELF correctness and GPU execution details.

## Web UI

1. Open **RULEST → Input files** and upload a **Custom seed rules file**, or
   choose a previously saved rule file from the library.
2. Open **Rule selection** and enable **Inject custom seed file into CELF**.
3. Set the maximum number of imported rules. The default is 1,000; raise it to
   any positive integer appropriate for the candidate file.
4. Run RULEST with the greedy selection mode.

The upload and saved-library selectors in Rule selection are synchronized with
the matching controls in Input files. The same selected file is reused; it is
not uploaded twice. The file must still satisfy the import validation above.
